Define a mortality rule stream

Source: R/mortality_rules.R
mortality_rule.Rd

Wraps a function so that detect_mortality() can run it beside the default streams of mortality_rules(). Add the result to that list.

Usage

mortality_rule(
  name,
  fun,
  kind = c("vote", "censor", "evidence", "rank"),
  settings = list(),
  label = name
)

Arguments

name

Name of the stream, used in the votes and on the cards.

fun

The function, as above.

kind

How the bands read the votes: "vote" (a dead vote is death evidence and an alive vote is alive evidence), "censor" (a review vote says the record ends where the rules cannot see), "evidence" (shown on the cards, never decides) or "rank" (the score orders the review band).

settings

A named list passed to fun.

label

Short label for the cards.

Value

An object of class mortality_rule.

Details

fun(data, settings) receives settings and a list data built once per run: x, the detection set; detections, the located detections of animals, with animal_id, transmitter, datetime, date, station_id, lat, lon and site; records, one row per animal with detections, n_days, first, last, located, tag_end, horizon, expected_end and end_basis; horizon, the data horizon, and record_end, the last detection in x; readings, the sensor readings with class, calibrated value and step, one count of the sensor on the calibrated scale; sites; sites_km; and votes, the votes of the streams that ran before it. The tables are data.table objects.

It returns a data frame with one row per animal it judges: animal_id, vote (one of "dead", "alive", "review", "none" or "unavailable"), and optionally score, date (POSIXct in UTC, the candidate death date), basis (what the date is) and detail (why). It may instead return a list of that data frame as votes and the rows behind them as evidence. Animals it leaves out get "unavailable".

See also

mortality_rules()

Examples

# A stream that sends every animal heard on fewer than 3 days to review.
few_days <- mortality_rule("few_days", function(data, settings) {
  records <- data$records
  data.frame(animal_id = records$animal_id,
             vote = ifelse(records$n_days < settings$days, "review", "none"))
}, settings = list(days = 3))
rules <- mortality_rules()
rules$few_days <- few_days
study <- example_mortality
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
table(detect_mortality(dets, rules)$bands$deciding_rule)
#> 
#> sparse_record 
#>             4
